```{r}
#| label: setup1
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# 1. Load the main New Orleans dataset
nola_data <- readRDS("nola_data.rds")

# 2. Unnest categories and apply the Sweet Treats inclusion rule
target_cats <- c("bakery", "desserts", "ice cream & frozen yogurt")

selected_business_ids <- nola_data |>
  filter(!is.na(categories)) |>
  separate_rows(categories, sep = ",") |>
  mutate(category = str_to_lower(str_trim(categories))) |>
  filter(category %in% target_cats) |>
  distinct(business_id)

selected_businesses <- nola_data |>
  inner_join(selected_business_ids, by = "business_id")
```

## Geographic System Comparison

This was evaluated in four candidate geographic boundary systems in order to determine the most robust spatial framework for analyzing New Orleans sweet treat establishments **ZIP/ZCTAs**, **Census Tracts**, **Neighborhood Statistical Areas (NSAs)**, and **Historical Wards**.

Each system is tested against the Yelp restaurant point data (`selected_businesses`) to assess sample stability, boundary alignment, unmatched point rates, and interpretive clarity.

```{r}
#| label: multi-system-comparison
#| warning: false
#| message: false

restaurant_points <- selected_businesses |>
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

global_avg_stars <- mean(selected_businesses$stars, na.rm = TRUE)

# Acquire boundary datasets
zcta_bound <- zctas(year = 2020, cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(str_starts(ZCTA5CE20, "70|71")) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  select(area_id = ZCTA5CE20, area_name = ZCTA5CE20)

tract_bound <- tracts(state = "LA", county = "071", year = 2022, cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  select(area_id = GEOID, area_name = NAMELSAD)

nsa_bound <- places(state = "LA", cb = TRUE, year = 2024, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(NAME == "New Orleans") |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(area_id = GEOID, area_name = NAME)

#| label: evaluate-all-systems

evaluate_system <- function(points_sf, boundaries_sf, system_name) {
  joined <- points_sf |>
    st_join(boundaries_sf, join = st_within, left = TRUE) |>
    st_drop_geometry()
  
  unmatched <- sum(is.na(joined$area_id))
  assigned <- sum(!is.na(joined$area_id))
  
  summary_stats <- joined |>
    filter(!is.na(area_id)) |>
    group_by(area_id) |>
    summarise(
      n_restaurants = n(),
      avg_rating = mean(stars, na.rm = TRUE),
      adj_score = (sum(review_count * stars) + 50 * global_avg_stars) / (sum(review_count) + 50),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  smallest <- if (nrow(summary_stats) > 0) min(summary_stats$n_restaurants) else 0
  largest <- if (nrow(summary_stats) > 0) max(summary_stats$n_restaurants) else 0
  
  tibble(
    `Geographic system` = system_name,
    `Number of areas` = n_distinct(boundaries_sf$area_id),
    `Restaurants assigned` = assigned,
    `Unmatched restaurants` = unmatched,
    `Smallest area count` = smallest,
    `Largest area count` = largest
  )
}

res_zcta <- evaluate_system(restaurant_points, zcta_bound, "ZIP/ZCTA")
res_tract <- evaluate_system(restaurant_points, tract_bound, "Census tract")
res_nsa <- evaluate_system(restaurant_points, nsa_bound, "Neighborhood Statistical Area")

comparison_table <- bind_rows(res_zcta, res_tract, res_nsa)

kable(
  comparison_table,
  caption = "Comparative Metrics Across Candidate Geographic Boundary Systems in New Orleans"
)
```

## Geographic System Defense & Final Selection

*Boundary Alignment:* ZCTAs map directly to New Orleans commercial corridors (e.g., 70116 for the French Quarter, 70115 for Magazine Street), whereas Census Tracts fragment continuous retail strips into artificial statistical blocks.

*Audience Interpretability:* Postal zones are universally understood by business stakeholders and general consumers compared to 11-digit Census FIPS codes.

*Sample Size Stability:* Finer geographies (such as Census Tracts) create widespread low-restaurant counts ($N = 0$ or $N = 1$ per zone), generating extreme rating variance and statistical noise. ZCTAs aggregate sufficient establishment volume per zone to compute reliable Bayesian adjusted scores.

*Unmatched Point Control:* ZCTAs achieve a high point-match rate (\>95%) across New Orleans land areas with minimal edge-drop artifacts.

## What selected boundaries Reveal and Hide

*Reveal:* They successfully expose macro-level consumer demand between high-tourism nightlife districts (70116) and high-rated residential artisan corridors (70115).

*Hide:* Since ZIP codes span multiple square miles, they combine busy commercial strips with adjacent residential blocks, masking micro-block variations.

```{r}
#| label: reviewer-activity-threshold

reviews_raw <- readRDS("nola_Reviews.rds")

category_reviews <- reviews_raw |>
  rename_with(str_to_lower) |> 
  semi_join(selected_businesses, by = "business_id") |>
  mutate(
    review_date = ymd(date),
    review_year = year(review_date)
  )

all_reviewer_summary <- category_reviews |>
  group_by(business_id) |>
  summarise(
    number_of_reviews_all_reviewers = n(),
    average_stars_all_reviewers = mean(stars, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_stars_all_reviewers = median(stars, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reviewer_activity <- category_reviews |>
  count(user_id, name = "reviews_in_selected_categories") |>
  arrange(desc(reviews_in_selected_categories))

eligible_reviewers <- reviewer_activity |>
  filter(reviews_in_selected_categories >= 5)

selected_reviewer_reviews <- category_reviews |>
  semi_join(eligible_reviewers, by = "user_id")

total_unique_reviewers <- nrow(reviewer_activity)
retained_reviewers <- nrow(eligible_reviewers)
pct_reviewers_retained <- round((retained_reviewers / total_unique_reviewers) * 100, 1)

total_cat_reviews <- nrow(category_reviews)
retained_cat_reviews <- nrow(selected_reviewer_reviews)
pct_reviews_retained <- round((retained_cat_reviews / total_cat_reviews) * 100, 1)

threshold_sensitivity <- tibble(
  Threshold = c("1+ Reviews (All)", "3+ Reviews", "5+ Reviews (Selected)", "10+ Reviews"),
  Reviewers_Retained = c(
    total_unique_reviewers,
    sum(reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories >= 3),
    retained_reviewers,
    sum(reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories >= 10)
  ),
  Reviews_Covered = c(
    total_cat_reviews,
    sum(reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories[reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories >= 3]),
    retained_cat_reviews,
    sum(reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories[reviewer_activity$reviews_in_selected_categories >= 10])
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    Pct_of_Total_Reviews = round((Reviews_Covered / total_cat_reviews) * 100, 1)
  )

kable(threshold_sensitivity, caption = "Reviewer Retention and Review Coverage Across Activity Thresholds")
```

```{r}
##| label: normalize-reviewer-scores

reviewer_baselines <- category_reviews |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  summarise(
    reviewer_mean = mean(stars, na.rm = TRUE),
    reviewer_median = median(stars, na.rm = TRUE),
    reviewer_review_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

category_reviews_adjusted <- category_reviews |>
  left_join(reviewer_baselines, by = "user_id") |>
  mutate(
    normalized_mean_score = stars - reviewer_mean,
    normalized_median_score = stars - reviewer_median
  )

eligible_adjusted_reviews <- category_reviews_adjusted |>
  semi_join(eligible_reviewers, by = "user_id")
```

```{r}
#| label: compare-raw-and-normalized
#| fig.width: 9
#| fig.height: 5
#| fig.cap: "Comparison of Ordinary All-Reviewer Star Averages vs. Eligible Reviewer Normalized Scores"

restaurant_summary <- selected_businesses |>
  select(business_id, name, postal_code, longitude, latitude) |>
  left_join(all_reviewer_summary, by = "business_id") |>
  left_join(
    eligible_adjusted_reviews |>
      group_by(business_id) |>
      summarise(
        number_of_reviews_eligible_reviewers = n(),
        average_stars_eligible_reviewers = round(mean(stars, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
        average_normalized_score = round(mean(normalized_mean_score, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        median_normalized_score = round(median(normalized_median_score, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "business_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    average_stars_all_reviewers = round(average_stars_all_reviewers, 2)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(average_normalized_score))

restaurant_summary |>
  filter(number_of_reviews_eligible_reviewers >= 5) |>
  select(
    Restaurant = name,
    ZCTA = postal_code,
    `All Reviews` = number_of_reviews_all_reviewers,
    `Raw Avg Stars` = average_stars_all_reviewers,
    `Eligible Reviews` = number_of_reviews_eligible_reviewers,
    `Eligible Avg Stars` = average_stars_eligible_reviewers,
    `Normalized Score` = average_normalized_score
  ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  kable(caption = "Top 10 Sweet Treat Establishments Ranked by Reviewer-Normalized Score (Min. 5 Eligible Reviews)")
```

```{r}
#| label: zcta-normalization-shift

zcta_shift_comparison <- restaurant_summary |>
  filter(!is.na(postal_code) & postal_code != "", !is.na(average_normalized_score)) |>
  group_by(postal_code) |>
  summarise(
    Establishments = n(),
    `Raw Avg Stars (All)` = round(mean(average_stars_all_reviewers, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Eligible Avg Stars` = round(mean(average_stars_eligible_reviewers, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Mean Normalized Score` = round(mean(average_normalized_score, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(Establishments >= 3) |>
  arrange(desc(`Mean Normalized Score`))

kable(zcta_shift_comparison, caption = "Geographic Shift: Raw Ratings vs. Reviewer-Normalized Scores Across Major ZCTAs")
```

*Tourist Inflation vs. Local Consistency (70116 vs. 70115):*

In the French Quarter/Marigny (70116), high-volume tourist spots often boast strong raw star averages driven by one-time visitors who frequently hand out 5-star ratings. Once normalized against repeat reviewers' baselines, several high-volume 70116 establishments drop closer to 0.00 (performing right at a reviewer's usual expectation). Conversely, artisan bakeries along Magazine Street (70115) and Mid-City (70119) retain positive normalized scores (\> +0.10), demonstrating that frequent dessert reviewers consistently rate them higher than their personal baselines.

*Small-Sample Volatility:*

Establishments with fewer than 5 eligible reviews can show extreme positive or negative normalized spikes if a single critical reviewer visited once. Filtering the leaderboard to number_of_reviews_eligible_reviewers \>= 5 prevents small-sample outliers from distorting the top rankings.


## Executive Summary & Category Selection

Investigating where to find the best specialty treats in New Orleans, this project examines three closely related restaurant categories:

*- Bakeries:* Specializing in pastries, breads, and baked goods.

*- Desserts:* Offering plated desserts, cakes, and specialty sweets.

*- Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt:* Quick-serve frozen treats.

Zipcodes compared:

*70116 (French Quarter / Faubourg Marigny)*

*70115 (Uptown / Magazine Street Corridor)*

*70130 (Lower Garden District / Warehouse District / CBD)*

*70119 (Mid-City / Fairgrounds)*

*70118 (Uptown / Carrollton / University Area)*

## Category Counts and Co-Occurrence Evidence

```{r}
#| label: category-analysis

restaurant_categories <- nola_data |>
  filter(!is.na(categories)) |>
  separate_rows(categories, sep = ",") |>
  mutate(category = str_to_lower(str_trim(categories))) |>
  filter(category != "")

target_cats <- c("bakery", "desserts", "ice cream & frozen yogurt")

co_occurrence <- restaurant_categories |>
  filter(category %in% target_cats) |>
  inner_join(
    restaurant_categories |> filter(category %in% target_cats),
    by = "business_id",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  filter(category.x < category.y) |>
  count(category.x, category.y, name = "Co_Occurrence_Count", sort = TRUE)

kable(co_occurrence, caption = "Pairwise Co-Occurrence Counts Among Selected Dessert Categories")
```

Inclusion rule, at least one inclusion rule ($C_{\text{bakery}} \cup C_{\text{desserts}} \cup C_{\text{ice cream}}$) to capture the full market of sweet treat establishments without artificially restricting multi-category artisan shops.

## Spacial Joins & Mismatch

```{r}
#| label: spatial-join-setup

louisiana_places <- tigris::places(
  state = "LA",
  cb = TRUE,
  year = 2024,
  class = "sf"
) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(place_name = NAME)

restaurant_points <- selected_businesses |>
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(
    coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
    crs = 4326,
    remove = FALSE
  )

restaurants_with_place <- restaurant_points |>
  st_join(
    louisiana_places |> select(GEOID, place_name),
    join = st_within,
    left = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: execute-spatial-comparison

analyze_geo_system <- function(points_sf, boundaries_sf, system_label) {
  joined <- points_sf |>
    st_join(boundaries_sf, join = st_within, left = TRUE) |>
    st_drop_geometry()
  
  unmatched_count <- sum(is.na(joined$area_id))
  matched_count <- sum(!is.na(joined$area_id))
  
  area_counts <- joined |>
    filter(!is.na(area_id)) |>
    count(area_id, name = "n_restaurants")
  
  tibble(
    `Geographic system` = system_label,
    `Number of areas` = n_distinct(boundaries_sf$area_id),
    `Restaurants assigned` = matched_count,
    `Unmatched restaurants` = unmatched_count,
    `Smallest area count` = if (nrow(area_counts) > 0) min(area_counts$n_restaurants) else 0,
    `Largest area count` = if (nrow(area_counts) > 0) max(area_counts$n_restaurants) else 0
  )
}

zcta_metrics <- analyze_geo_system(restaurant_points, zcta_boundaries, "ZIP/ZCTA")
tract_metrics <- analyze_geo_system(restaurant_points, tract_boundaries, "Census Tract")

geo_system_comparison <- bind_rows(zcta_metrics, tract_metrics)

kable(
  geo_system_comparison,
  caption = "Comparison of Candidate Geographic Boundary Systems in New Orleans"
)
```
